"""Verify retained browser pixels/identities; visual and family judgments are separate."""

import argparse
import json
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path
from typing import cast

from PIL import Image, ImageChops, ImageColor


def digest(path):
    return sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def rgb_difference(left, right):
    extrema = cast(tuple[tuple[float, float], ...], ImageChops.difference(left, right).convert("RGB").getextrema())
    return max(high for low, high in extrema)


def confined(root, name):
    path = (root / name).resolve()
    if not path.is_relative_to(root.resolve()):
        raise ValueError("Capture resource escapes its root")
    return path


def check(project, capture):
    project, capture = Path(project).resolve(), Path(capture).resolve()
    report = json.loads((capture / "render.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    failures, observations = [], []

    def expect(condition, name):
        observations.append({"check": name, "pass": bool(condition)})
        if not condition:
            failures.append(name)

    def retained_image(reference):
        path = confined(capture, reference["path"])
        expect(digest(path) == reference["sha256"], "retained image hash: " + reference["path"])
        with Image.open(path) as image:
            return image.convert("RGBA")

    expect(not report["errors"], "browser reported no script errors")
    expect(report["devicePixelRatio"] == 1, "capture declares device pixel ratio one")
    for name, expected in report.get("renderer_files", {}).items():
        expect(digest(confined(Path(__file__).resolve().parent, name)) == expected, "renderer implementation: " + name)
    for name, expected in report["served_files"].items():
        group, relative = name.split("/", 1)
        base = project if group == "consumer" else Path(__file__).resolve().parent
        path = confined(base, relative)
        expect(digest(path) == expected, "served bytes: " + name)
    screenshot = retained_image(report["screenshot"])
    if "viewport" in report:
        expect(screenshot.size == (report["viewport"]["width"], report["viewport"]["height"]), "screenshot and observed viewport dimensions")
    width, height = report["display"]["cell"]
    background = ImageColor.getrgb(report["display"]["background"])
    available = []
    for view in report["views"]:
        if not view["asset"]["available"]:
            expect("image" not in view, "missing asset has no invented view: " + view["state"])
            continue
        actual = retained_image(view["image"])
        available.append(view)
        label = f"{view['consumer']} {view['state']} {view['scale']}x"
        scale = view["scale"]
        bounds = view["bounds"]
        expect(view["geometryMatches"], label + " source sheet geometry")
        expect(view["smoothing"] is False and view["imageRendering"] == "pixelated", label + " nearest sampling settings")
        expect(actual.size == (width * scale, height * scale), label + " actual canvas dimensions")
        expect(all(value == int(value) for value in bounds.values()), label + " integer destination bounds")
        x, y = int(bounds["x"]), int(bounds["y"])
        on_screen = screenshot.crop((x, y, x + actual.width, y + actual.height))
        expect(ImageChops.difference(on_screen, actual).convert("RGB").getbbox() is None, label + " screenshot matches canvas pixels")
        source = confined(project, view["descriptor"]["path"])
        expect(digest(source) == view["asset"]["sha256"], label + " actual asset identity")
        if source.suffix.lower() == ".png":
            with Image.open(source) as image:
                expect(image.size == (width * view["descriptor"]["frames"], height), label + " independently decoded sheet size")
                frame = image.convert("RGBA").crop((view["frame"] * width, 0, (view["frame"] + 1) * width, height))
            expected = Image.alpha_composite(Image.new("RGBA", frame.size, (*background, 255)), frame).resize(actual.size, Image.Resampling.NEAREST)
            expect(rgb_difference(expected, actual) <= 1, label + " source pixels and alpha compositing (rounding tolerance one)")
        if scale != 1 and source.suffix.lower() == ".png":
            base = next(v for v in report["views"] if v["consumer"] == view["consumer"] and v["state"] == view["state"] and v["scale"] == 1)
            native = retained_image(base["image"]).resize(actual.size, Image.Resampling.NEAREST)
            expect(ImageChops.difference(native, actual).convert("RGB").getbbox() is None, label + " nearest pixel blocks")
    for sample in report["timeline"]:
        if not sample["available"]:
            expect(sample["frame"] is None and "image" not in sample, "missing animation is not a playback result")
            continue
        descriptor = next(v["descriptor"] for v in report["views"] if v["state"] == sample["state"])
        frame_index = (sample["elapsed"] // report["display"]["frameMs"]) % descriptor["frames"]
        expect(sample["frame"] == frame_index, f"frame boundary at {sample['elapsed']}ms")
        actual = retained_image(sample["image"])
        with Image.open(confined(project, descriptor["path"])) as image:
            frame = image.convert("RGBA").crop((frame_index * width, 0, (frame_index + 1) * width, height))
        expected = Image.alpha_composite(Image.new("RGBA", frame.size, (*background, 255)), frame)
        expect(rgb_difference(expected, actual) <= 1, f"decoded frame crop at {sample['elapsed']}ms")
    return {"version": 1, "status": "pass" if not failures else "fail", "capture_sha256": digest(capture / "render.json"), "observations": observations, "failures": failures,
            "available_views": len(available), "missing": report["missing"],
            "scope": "Identities, observed DOM/canvas dimensions, screenshot pixel correspondence, PNG alpha compositing, nearest blocks and available frame-boundary crops. Not an artistic/style verdict or acceptance of absent members; sampled frame boundaries are not a review of animation quality."}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--project", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--capture", type=Path, required=True)

10	
11	Open the exact nominated sample X and its retained observations. Confirm its sample task is done and that its passing verdicts answer the family-relevant question. A replaced or rejected candidate cannot serve as the approved baseline merely because its old PNG remains. 12	
13	When a corrected contract follows an earlier delivery, identify which review actually
14	adopts the sample for this family. Preserve the earlier contract/verdicts; evaluate
15	the retained bytes against the new saved criteria before claiming new acceptance.
16	The same image can remain useful without another generation. Record the baseline's
17	exact identity, the caller's scoped style decision and which properties carry into
18	later members. A completion glyph may establish edge treatment and color roles; it
19	does not prescribe the other members' silhouettes or prove their motion/meaning.
20	The caller may resolve expert design choices within its delegated assignment; do
21	not invent a separate owner approval when that authority was already supplied.
22	
23	Inventory available and missing members before collective review. A sample decision
24	and a comparison with an existing control can be complete while the family remains
25	unfinished. Keep missing members planned, with concrete next work; do not create a
26	passing family snapshot or silently remove them from the family to finish a report.
27	
28	## Save the members and collective requirements first
29	
30	Use the normal decode/edit/encode/validate/expected-hash commit sequence. Record only fields defined in the current specification. Before files exist, save F plans rather than invented X identities.
31	
32	1. Each production F names the exact sample candidate through `bs`. Its producer T lists that X in `ip` and the sample T directly in `dp`. Retain the applicable contract, confirmed choices, adoption D and executed proof; the baseline link does not replace those requirements.

34	3. Define member Q criteria and separate collective Q criteria before results. The family needs a continuity criterion with an observable condition and appropriate evidence mode. State the actual comparison: for example, consistent equipment placement across the requested directions, grounded feet across the cycle, or matching shared boundaries across the required tile transitions. Add engine criteria when required by this destination; a target name alone does not create an engine verdict.
35	4. Missing choices remain unresolved; observed/proposed values remain distinct from confirmation. Such choices block delivery activation/completion, while useful member files can still be retained.
36	
37	Commit this plan before collecting verdicts. Keep the project's actual dimensions, style and acceptance conditions; example values are not defaults. `ready` and `workflow` apply activation blockers. 38	
39	## Produce members, compare them, and preserve rejection
40	
41	Run the [provider recovery operation](provider-recovery.md) for each required real generation attempt. It saves the exact request before dispatch and imports actual downloaded bytes as an unaccepted candidate. Read the family report as well as jobs: a member or baseline attempt may be outside the delivery task's forward context packet. 42

44

46	| --- | --- |

56

69

71	
72	Use the target engine and the retained files to exercise the applicable import behavior: frame slicing and order, pivots/contact alignment, timing and loop transitions, direction mapping, texture sampling/display scale, alpha/atlas edges, tile neighbor mapping, or required material/lighting behavior. 73	
74	Exercise the real consumer path, including backend transitions and every assigned
75	shared view, rather than drawing the asset in an unrelated preview. If an existing
76	representative fixture only supplies source descriptors, an explicitly scoped
77	graphical entry point can make those modules executable. Bind captures to the
78	actual modules, image bytes and renderer version; report this fixture's observed
79	behavior without claiming another project's engine acceptance. Preserve missing
80	or failed states visibly. Browser screenshots, pixel/compositing measurements and
81	the specialist's visual judgment answer different questions; retain each as needed.
82

An N record can point to the retained records/tasks; retain the human-readable instructions in project evidence as needed.

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
47	
48	## Specialist → caller while working
49	
50	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
51	
52	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
53	
54	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
55	
56	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
57	
58	## Specialist → caller at completion
59	
60	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields):
61	
62	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
63	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
64	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
65	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
66	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
67	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
68	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
69	
70	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
71	
72	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
73	
74	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
75	
76	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
77	
78	For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
79	use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`, production `hash` as
80	`expect`, and your `details` object. CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --asset ID
81	--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
82	complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
83	Return that file's path/hash as `handoff`; the caller opens it and compares its state
84	identity with fresh focused PLAR. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
85	Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
86	
87	`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
88	expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
89	caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
90	`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
91	runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
92	The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
93	does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.
94	
95	On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
96	requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
97	its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
98	actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
99	explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.
100	
101	Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.
102

**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.

For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields):

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`, production `hash` as
`expect`, and your `details` object. CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --asset ID
--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
Return that file's path/hash as `handoff`; the caller opens it and compares its state
identity with fresh focused PLAR. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.

`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.

On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.

Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.

# locate each available view canvas inside the screenshot by exhaustive search near expected bounds
import numpy as np

    img=np.array(Image.open('work/render-caller-01/'+v['image']['path']).convert('RGBA'))[:,:,:3].astype(int)
    h,w=img.shape[:2]
    bx,by=int(v['bounds']['x']),int(v['bounds']['y'])
    best=None
    for dy in range(-60,61):
        for dx in range(-60,61):
            x,y=bx+dx,by+dy
            if x<0 or y<0 or x+w>S.shape[1] or y+h>S.shape[0]: continue
            d=np.abs(S[y:y+h,x:x+w]-img).max()

import json
from PIL import Image, ImageChops
cap='work/render-caller-01/'
r=json.load(open(cap+'render.json'))
shot=Image.open(cap+'destination.png').convert('RGB')
out=[]
for v in r['views']:
    if not v['asset']['available']: continue
    img=Image.open(cap+v['image']['path']).convert('RGB')
    w,h=img.size; bx,by=int(v['bounds']['x']),int(v['bounds']['y'])
    best=None
    for dy in range(-24,25):
        for dx in range(-24,25):
            x,y=bx+dx,by+dy
            if x<0 or y<0 or x+w>shot.width or y+h>shot.height: continue
            ext=ImageChops.difference(shot.crop((x,y,x+w,y+h)),img).getextrema()
            d=max(e[1] for e in ext)
            if best is None or d<best[0]: best=(d,dx,dy)
    label=f"{v['consumer']} {v['state']} {v['scale']}x"
    out.append({'view':label,'image':v['image']['path'],'reported_bounds':[bx,by,w,h],'best_match':{'max_channel_diff':best[0],'dx':best[1],'dy':best[2]}})
    print(label,'reported',(bx,by),'best',best)
# ready view colours and composite comparison
src=Image.open('assets/ready-confirmed.png').convert('RGBA')
comp=Image.alpha_composite(Image.new('RGBA',src.size,(0x17,0x23,0x36,255)),src)
for name,ref in [('view-004.png',comp),('view-006.png',comp),('view-005.png',comp.resize((48,48),Image.NEAREST)),('view-007.png',comp.resize((48,48),Image.NEAREST))]:
    im=Image.open(cap+name).convert('RGBA')
    print(name,im.size,'colours',sorted(im.getcolors()),'diff bbox vs independent composite',ImageChops.difference(ref,im).getbbox())
for name in ['view-000.png','view-001.png']:
    im=Image.open(cap+name).convert('RGBA'); cs=im.getcolors(10000); print(name,im.size,'distinct colours',len(cs),'top',sorted(cs,reverse=True)[:5])
json.dump({'capture':'work/render-caller-01','screenshot_size':list(shot.size),'reported_viewport':r['viewport'],'canvas_search':out},open('work/render-stage-review/screenshot-offset-search.json','w'),indent=2)
EOF

1	"""Verify retained browser pixels/identities; visual and family judgments are separate."""
2	
3	import argparse
4	import json
5	from hashlib import sha256
6	from pathlib import Path
7	from typing import cast
8	
9	from PIL import Image, ImageChops, ImageColor
10	
11	
12	def digest(path):
13	    return sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
14	
15	
16	def rgb_difference(left, right):
17	    extrema = cast(tuple[tuple[float, float], ...], ImageChops.difference(left, right).convert("RGB").getextrema())
18	    return max(high for low, high in extrema)
19	
20	
21	def confined(root, name):
22	    path = (root / name).resolve()
23	    if not path.is_relative_to(root.resolve()):
24	        raise ValueError("Capture resource escapes its root")
25	    return path
26	
27	
28	def check(project, capture):
29	    project, capture = Path(project).resolve(), Path(capture).resolve()
30	    report = json.loads((capture / "render.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
31	    failures, observations = [], []
32	
33	    def expect(condition, name):
34	        observations.append({"check": name, "pass": bool(condition)})
35	        if not condition:
36	            failures.append(name)
37	
38	    def retained_image(reference):
39	        path = confined(capture, reference["path"])
40	        expect(digest(path) == reference["sha256"], "retained image hash: " + reference["path"])
41	        with Image.open(path) as image:
42	            return image.convert("RGBA")
43	
44	    expect(not report["errors"], "browser reported no script errors")
45	    expect(report["devicePixelRatio"] == 1, "capture declares device pixel ratio one")
46	    for name, expected in report.get("renderer_files", {}).items():
47	        expect(digest(confined(Path(__file__).resolve().parent, name)) == expected, "renderer implementation: " + name)
48	    for name, expected in report["served_files"].items():
49	        group, relative = name.split("/", 1)
50	        base = project if group == "consumer" else Path(__file__).resolve().parent
51	        path = confined(base, relative)
52	        expect(digest(path) == expected, "served bytes: " + name)
53	    screenshot = retained_image(report["screenshot"])
54	    if "viewport" in report:
55	        expect(screenshot.size == (report["viewport"]["width"], report["viewport"]["height"]), "screenshot and observed viewport dimensions")
56	    width, height = report["display"]["cell"]
57	    background = ImageColor.getrgb(report["display"]["background"])
58	    available = []
59	    for view in report["views"]:
60	        if not view["asset"]["available"]:
61	            expect("image" not in view, "missing asset has no invented view: " + view["state"])
62	            continue
63	        actual = retained_image(view["image"])
64	        available.append(view)
65	        label = f"{view['consumer']} {view['state']} {view['scale']}x"
66	        scale = view["scale"]
67	        bounds = view["bounds"]
68	        expect(view["geometryMatches"], label + " source sheet geometry")
69	        expect(view["smoothing"] is False and view["imageRendering"] == "pixelated", label + " nearest sampling settings")
70	        expect(actual.size == (width * scale, height * scale), label + " actual canvas dimensions")
71	        expect(all(value == int(value) for value in bounds.values()), label + " integer destination bounds")
72	        x, y = int(bounds["x"]), int(bounds["y"])
73	        on_screen = screenshot.crop((x, y, x + actual.width, y + actual.height))
74	        expect(ImageChops.difference(on_screen, actual).convert("RGB").getbbox() is None, label + " screenshot matches canvas pixels")
75	        source = confined(project, view["descriptor"]["path"])
76	        expect(digest(source) == view["asset"]["sha256"], label + " actual asset identity")
77	        if source.suffix.lower() == ".png":
78	            with Image.open(source) as image:
79	                expect(image.size == (width * view["descriptor"]["frames"], height), label + " independently decoded sheet size")
80	                frame = image.convert("RGBA").crop((view["frame"] * width, 0, (view["frame"] + 1) * width, height))
81	            expected = Image.alpha_composite(Image.new("RGBA", frame.size, (*background, 255)), frame).resize(actual.size, Image.Resampling.NEAREST)
82	            expect(rgb_difference(expected, actual) <= 1, label + " source pixels and alpha compositing (rounding tolerance one)")
83	        if scale != 1 and source.suffix.lower() == ".png":
84	            base = next(v for v in report["views"] if v["consumer"] == view["consumer"] and v["state"] == view["state"] and v["scale"] == 1)
85	            native = retained_image(base["image"]).resize(actual.size, Image.Resampling.NEAREST)
86	            expect(ImageChops.difference(native, actual).convert("RGB").getbbox() is None, label + " nearest pixel blocks")
87	    for sample in report["timeline"]:
88	        if not sample["available"]:
89	            expect(sample["frame"] is None and "image" not in sample, "missing animation is not a playback result")
90	            continue
91	        descriptor = next(v["descriptor"] for v in report["views"] if v["state"] == sample["state"])
92	        frame_index = (sample["elapsed"] // report["display"]["frameMs"]) % descriptor["frames"]
93	        expect(sample["frame"] == frame_index, f"frame boundary at {sample['elapsed']}ms")
94	        actual = retained_image(sample["image"])
95	        with Image.open(confined(project, descriptor["path"])) as image:
96	            frame = image.convert("RGBA").crop((frame_index * width, 0, (frame_index + 1) * width, height))
97	        expected = Image.alpha_composite(Image.new("RGBA", frame.size, (*background, 255)), frame)
98	        expect(rgb_difference(expected, actual) <= 1, f"decoded frame crop at {sample['elapsed']}ms")
99	    return {"version": 1, "status": "pass" if not failures else "fail", "capture_sha256": digest(capture / "render.json"), "observations": observations, "failures": failures,
100	            "available_views": len(available), "missing": report["missing"],
101	            "scope": "Identities, observed DOM/canvas dimensions, screenshot pixel correspondence, PNG alpha compositing, nearest blocks and available frame-boundary crops. Not an artistic/style verdict or acceptance of absent members; sampled frame boundaries are not a review of animation quality."}
102	
103	
104	if __name__ == "__main__":
105	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
106	    parser.add_argument("--project", type=Path, required=True)
107	    parser.add_argument("--capture", type=Path, required=True)
108	    args = parser.parse_args()
109	    result = check(args.project, args.capture)
110	    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
111	    raise SystemExit(0 if result["status"] == "pass" else 1)
112

"""Independent measurements of the render-pixl-01 capture (specialist diagnostics; not art, not acceptance)."""
import json
import sys
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageChops

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
CAP = ROOT / "work/render-pixl-01"
OUT = ROOT / "work/render-stage-pixl"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
PANEL = (0x17, 0x23, 0x36)
ACCENT = (0x70, 0xB9, 0xED)


def digest(p):
    return sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def max_diff(a, b):
    ext = ImageChops.difference(a.convert("RGB"), b.convert("RGB")).getextrema()
    return max(h for _, h in ext)


report = json.loads((CAP / "render.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
shot = Image.open(CAP / "destination.png").convert("RGB")
result = {"capture": "work/render-pixl-01", "screenshot": {"size": list(shot.size), "sha256": digest(CAP / "destination.png")},

# body is `max-width: 1120px; margin: auto` so a wider layout viewport re-centres content horizontally

    "body_max_width_px": 1120, "body_margin": "auto",
    "left_margin_at_reported_width": (report["viewport"]["width"] - 1120) // 2,
    "left_margin_at_screenshot_width": (shot.size[0] - 1120) // 2,
    "predicted_dx": (shot.size[0] - 1120) // 2 - (report["viewport"]["width"] - 1120) // 2,
    "predicted_dy": 0,
}

available = [v for v in report["views"] if v["asset"]["available"]]
for v in available:
    img = Image.open(CAP / v["image"]["path"]).convert("RGB")
    bx, by = int(v["bounds"]["x"]), int(v["bounds"]["y"])
    w, h = img.size
    at_reported = max_diff(shot.crop((bx, by, bx + w, by + h)), img)
    best = None
    for dy in range(-24, 25):
        for dx in range(-24, 25):
            x, y = bx + dx, by + dy
            if x < 0 or y < 0 or x + w > shot.size[0] or y + h > shot.size[1]:
                continue
            d = max_diff(shot.crop((x, y, x + w, y + h)), img)
            if best is None or d < best["max_channel_diff"] or (d == best["max_channel_diff"] and abs(dx) + abs(dy) < abs(best["dx"]) + abs(best["dy"])):
                best = {"max_channel_diff": d, "dx": dx, "dy": dy}
    sx, sy = bx + best["dx"], by + best["dy"]
    # label gap: scan right of the canvas along its full height for the first column with any non-panel pixel
    gap = None
    for col in range(sx + w, min(sx + w + 60, shot.size[0])):
        column = [shot.getpixel((col, yy)) for yy in range(sy, sy + h)]
        if any(p != PANEL for p in column):
            gap = col - (sx + w)
            break
    # label vertical extent (text pixels) within +-30 px of the canvas, in the 120 px to the right
    text_rows = []
    for yy in range(max(0, sy - 30), min(shot.size[1], sy + h + 30)):
        if any(shot.getpixel((xx, yy)) != PANEL for xx in range(sx + w + (gap or 0), min(shot.size[0], sx + w + (gap or 0) + 120))):
            text_rows.append(yy)
    colors = img.getcolors(maxcolors=4096)
    entry = {
        "view": f"{v['consumer']} {v['state']} {v['scale']}x", "image": v["image"]["path"], "sha256": v["image"]["sha256"],
        "sha256_recomputed": digest(CAP / v["image"]["path"]), "size": [w, h], "reported_bounds": [bx, by, w, h],
        "max_channel_diff_at_reported_bounds": at_reported, "best_match": best, "match_position": [sx, sy],
        "canvas_centre_y": sy + h / 2, "label_gap_px": gap, "label_text_rows": [min(text_rows), max(text_rows)] if text_rows else None,
        "label_centre_y": (min(text_rows) + max(text_rows) + 1) / 2 if text_rows else None,
        "distinct_colors": len(colors), "accent_pixels": sum(c for c, p in colors if p == ACCENT), "panel_pixels": sum(c for c, p in colors if p == PANEL),
        "other_pixels": sum(c for c, p in colors if p not in (ACCENT, PANEL)),
    }
    if v["descriptor"]["path"].endswith(".png"):
        src = Image.open(ROOT / v["descriptor"]["path"]).convert("RGBA")
        comp = Image.alpha_composite(Image.new("RGBA", src.size, (*PANEL, 255)), src).convert("RGB")
        expected = comp.resize(img.size, Image.Resampling.NEAREST) if v["scale"] != 1 else comp
        entry["max_channel_diff_vs_pillow_composite_nearest"] = max_diff(expected, img)
    result["views"].append(entry)

# Start vector: is the 3x canvas a nearest upscale of the 1x raster, or a re-rasterisation?
v1 = Image.open(CAP / "view-000.png").convert("RGB")
v3 = Image.open(CAP / "view-001.png").convert("RGB")
result["start_vector_raster"] = {
    "1x_colors": sorted("#%02x%02x%02x" % p for _, p in v1.getcolors(4096)),
    "3x_colors": sorted("#%02x%02x%02x" % p for _, p in v3.getcolors(4096)),
    "3x_equals_nearest_upscale_of_1x_max_diff": max_diff(v1.resize((48, 48), Image.Resampling.NEAREST), v3),
    "1x_intermediate_pixels": sum(c for c, p in v1.getcolors(4096) if p not in (ACCENT, PANEL)),
    "3x_intermediate_pixels": sum(c for c, p in v3.getcolors(4096) if p not in (ACCENT, PANEL)),
    "1x_triangle_bbox_nonpanel": ImageChops.difference(v1, Image.new("RGB", v1.size, PANEL)).getbbox(),
    "3x_triangle_bbox_nonpanel": ImageChops.difference(v3, Image.new("RGB", v3.size, PANEL)).getbbox(),
}

# Live panel: locate the two 3x Ready canvases in the top region by exact match against view-005
ready3 = Image.open(CAP / "view-005.png").convert("RGB")
for y in range(150, 300):
    for x in range(100, 600):
        if shot.getpixel((x, y)) == ACCENT and shot.getpixel((x - 1, y)) == PANEL and shot.getpixel((x, y - 1)) == PANEL:
            # candidate top-left of the mark at (x - 9, y - 12) inside a 48x48 canvas
            cx, cy = x - 9, y - 12
            if cx >= 0 and cy >= 0 and max_diff(shot.crop((cx, cy, cx + 48, cy + 48)), ready3) == 0:

# Ready fixture facts
fx = Image.open(ROOT / "assets/ready-confirmed.png").convert("RGBA")
px = fx.load()
opaque = [(x, y) for y in range(16) for x in range(16) if px[x, y][3] != 0]
rows = ["".join("#" if px[x, y][3] else "." for x in range(16)) for y in range(16)]
alphas = sorted({px[x, y][3] for y in range(16) for x in range(16)})
colors = sorted({px[x, y] for (x, y) in opaque})
xs, ys = [p[0] for p in opaque], [p[1] for p in opaque]
# 4-connected components
seen, comps = set(), 0
for p in opaque:
    if p in seen:
        continue
    comps += 1
    stack = [p]
    while stack:
        q = stack.pop()
        if q in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(q)
        for d in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
            n = (q[0] + d[0], q[1] + d[1])
            if n in opaque and n not in seen:
                stack.append(n)
runs = []
for y in range(16):
    run, cur = [], 0
    for x in range(16):
        if px[x, y][3]:
            cur += 1
        elif cur:
            run.append(cur); cur = 0
    if cur:
        run.append(cur)
    if run:
        runs.append({"row": y, "runs": run})


def lum(c):
    def ch(v):
        v /= 255
        return v / 12.92 if v <= 0.03928 else ((v + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4
    return 0.2126 * ch(c[0]) + 0.7152 * ch(c[1]) + 0.0722 * ch(c[2])


la, lp = lum(ACCENT), lum(PANEL)
result["ready_fixture"] = {

    "components_4_connected": comps, "visible_bbox_exclusive": [min(xs), min(ys), max(xs) + 1, max(ys) + 1],
    "bbox_size": [max(xs) + 1 - min(xs), max(ys) + 1 - min(ys)], "bbox_centre": [(min(xs) + max(xs) + 1) / 2, (min(ys) + max(ys) + 1) / 2],
    "mass_centroid": [round(sum(xs) / len(xs) + 0.5, 3), round(sum(ys) / len(ys) + 0.5, 3)],
    "pixel_map": rows, "row_runs": runs,
    "lowest_pixel": max(opaque, key=lambda p: (p[1], -p[0])),
    "left_arm_pixels_x_le_5": sum(1 for p in opaque if p[0] <= 5), "right_arm_pixels_x_ge_7": sum(1 for p in opaque if p[0] >= 7), "vertex_column_6_pixels": sum(1 for p in opaque if p[0] == 6),
    "left_arm_columns": [min(p[0] for p in opaque if p[0] <= 5), max(p[0] for p in opaque if p[0] <= 5)], "left_arm_rows": [min(p[1] for p in opaque if p[0] <= 5), max(p[1] for p in opaque if p[0] <= 5)],
    "right_arm_columns": [min(p[0] for p in opaque if p[0] >= 7), max(p[0] for p in opaque if p[0] >= 7)], "right_arm_rows": [min(p[1] for p in opaque if p[0] >= 7), max(p[1] for p in opaque if p[0] >= 7)],
    "wcag_contrast_accent_on_panel": round((max(la, lp) + 0.05) / (min(la, lp) + 0.05), 2),
    "luma_601_accent": round(0.299 * ACCENT[0] + 0.587 * ACCENT[1] + 0.114 * ACCENT[2], 1), "luma_601_panel": round(0.299 * PANEL[0] + 0.587 * PANEL[1] + 0.114 * PANEL[2], 1),
}

# Derived crops (diagnostic enlargements of the actual screenshot; not art)
def crop(name, box, scale):
    im = shot.crop(box).resize(((box[2] - box[0]) * scale, (box[3] - box[1]) * scale), Image.Resampling.NEAREST)
    p = OUT / name

    result["derived_crops"][name] = {"source": "work/render-pixl-01/destination.png", "box": list(box), "nearest_scale": scale, "size": list(im.size), "sha256": digest(p)}


dx = result["layout_shift_prediction"]["predicted_dx"]

1	# plar.txt format and operations
2	
3	Version 1 is UTF-8 JSON, not a new programming language. The normative shape is [plar.schema.json](../../../runtime/pixl/plar.schema.json). A complete worked project is [the queue UI example](../../../resources/examples/plar-project/README.md). Read its source before its example requirements.
4	
5	Top-level fields:
6	
7	| Field | Meaning |
8	| --- | --- |
9	| version | `1` |
10	| project | `name` and concise `brief`; no absolute installation paths |
11	| coverage | Arrays `included`, `excluded`, `unresolved`; explicit scan boundary and blind spots |
12	| sources | Stable `id`, project-relative `path`, optional `sha256`; saves bind existing files without a hash |
13	| assets | Stable rows described below; an empty list is valid when the inspected scope requires no production art |
14	
15	Each asset has `id`, `kind`, `purpose`, `status`, `consumers`, `existing`, `requirements`, `delivery`, `depends_on`, `questions`, `next`, and `evidence`. Optional `production` links `store`, `task`, `output`. Optional `references` names visual inputs as described below. Kind is a descriptive string; UI panels, fonts, atlases and normal maps need not pretend to be sprites here. Translate to the actual PIXL/provider contract during production.
16	
17	- `consumers`: `{source, symbol, usage}`; source is an ID from the sources table. Symbol and usage explain the binding, not merely a filename.
18	- `references`: `{source, role, instructions}`; source is a bound source ID. Role is `style`, `identity`, `pose`, `layout`, `palette`, `mask` or `motion`. Instructions say what to preserve. These are optional for text-only briefs; a filename mentioned in a requirement is not provider image transport.
19	- `existing`: `{path, role}`; role explains reusable/placeholder/reference or other current use. Missing paths are reported, not rejected.
20	- `requirements`: `{property, value, authority, sources, reason}`. Value is JSON; authority is `requirement`, `observation`, `proposal`, or `unknown`. Sources is an array of source IDs. An empty array is useful for an explicit unsourced proposal/unknown; support adopted requirements with addressable evidence.
21	- `delivery`: `{path, checks}`; exact destination (file or package path) and applicable mechanical, visual and consumer/import checks.
22	- `depends_on`: other asset IDs; cycles and dangling IDs are rejected.
23	- `questions`: unresolved choices relevant to this asset. `next`: one actionable instruction.
24	- `evidence`: `{path, note}` links to retained results. Source-bind evidence that must remain byte-identical.
25	- `status`: `todo`, `in_progress`, `review`, `integrated`, or `deferred`. Status is authored by the host. File existence does not prove integration or quality.
26	
27	All paths are relative to the consumer root and use forward slashes. Source hashes detect local drift; they do not prove the interpretation of the source. The reader reports changed/missing/unbound sources and missing files. It does not restamp changed sources, guess readiness, contact PixelLab or certify artistic quality. Refresh a hash only after re-reading and reconciling the dependent claims. Focused reads include the full transitive dependency rows and their issues, so a caller does not lose the style baseline or an unresolved source when delegating a dependent asset.
28	
29	## MCP
30	
31	`pixl_plar_read({})` returns the queue, project scope and source binding results. To select an asset:
32	
33	```json
34	{"asset_id":"queue.working"}
35	```
36	
37	Save through `pixl_plar_save` with `document` holding the complete JSON document and `expect` equal to the last returned file hash, or `"new"` for creation. Optional `path` defaults to `plar.txt`. A stale write is rejected; re-read and merge. Previous changed bytes are retained under `.pixl/plar-history/`. Keep independent queues in separate files when project scope requires it.
38	
39	Use `pixl_commit({store,expect,document})` for a PX2 document with its next revision. The JSON record format uses `{"$ref":"id"}` and `{"$symbol":"value"}`. Exactly one of `document` or the existing `candidate` wire-file path is accepted. The same revision, dependency, evidence and acceptance checks apply. PLAR does not automatically invent PX2 decisions or criteria.
40	
41	## CLI and portability
42	
43	Resolve the plugin runner relative to this skill, then use its **absolute** path with the target project root:
44	
45	```text
46	python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py plar read --root /ABS/PROJECT
47	python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py plar read --root /ABS/PROJECT --asset queue.working
48	python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py plar save /ABS/document.json --root /ABS/PROJECT --expect new
49	python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py commit /ABS/PROJECT/.pixl /ABS/plan.json --json --expect STATE_HASH --root /ABS/PROJECT
50	```
51	
52	Copy/install the complete plugin, not the skill directory alone. Requirements and outputs stay in the consumer project. The CLI can support a host without MCP; the MCP server exposes the same deterministic operations when configured with that root.
53	
54	## Focused delegation identity
55	
56	A selected read returns `project_root`, `requirements_hash`, `asset`, full `dependencies`, relevant `sources`, `visual_references` and a derived `production` view. Source rows add `observed_sha256` and `absolute_path`; stored source paths remain portable and relative. The full queue's existing `hash` is still the compare-and-swap token for saves.
57	
58	The requirements hash covers the selected asset and transitive dependency requirements, their bound/current source identities and project brief. It excludes status, next action, evidence lists, production-state links and absolute installation paths. It does not assert readiness or acceptance; read dependency status/issues separately. Changing a style reference changes this hash even before someone refreshes its saved source hash. An unrelated asset's queue progress does not.
59	
60	This additive version-1 extension keeps existing documents valid. Use a runtime containing the reference-role extension to author documents with `references`; older closed-schema readers cannot interpret new fields.
61	
62	## Selective refresh
63	
64	Queue reads include `changes`: tracked source drift, direct and transitively affected asset IDs, and unaffected IDs. Pass `since` (CLI `--since`) with a retained prior PLAR byte hash to compare declarations as well. Saves return this comparison against the replaced version. Queue progress fields (`status`, `next`, `evidence`, `production`) are not requirement changes. Coverage changes are reported separately. History bytes are hash-checked before comparison. Use `since` on the whole queue, then select an affected asset; focused reads include `dependency_issues`.
65	
66	This is conservative file/dependency impact, not a semantic code scanner. Re-read changed code and look for new states, consumers or dynamic paths. A shared source edit can affect several rows for review without requiring all their requirements or assets to change. Do not merely refresh hashes. Keep stable roles/IDs on destination moves; retain superseded work as deferred where applicable.
67	
68	[First-candidate preparation](prepare.md) consumes a focused selection and the exact reviewed request/criteria artifacts, removing handwritten PX2 setup from that path.
69	
70	## Allocation and production continuity
71	
72	A focused read joins the selected row to its retained PX2 store. `production` reports
73	current task/output acceptance, selection identity, provider-bound pending jobs and
74	one next action. Missing or invalid state is an explicit diagnostic while the
75	requirements remain readable. Queue `status` remains an authored progress label.
76	`new_request_allowed` is only a local selection/pending-work advisory; preparation
77	still validates the exact reviewed request, current source identity and connection.
78	
79	Single-output preparation links the resulting store/task/output and snapshot evidence
80	back to the row. A failed concurrent queue save leaves the prepared job intact; resume
81	the same preparation to repair its link. The default asset store is discoverable;
82	custom stores require the existing link or explicit store argument. Multiple outputs
83	need a deliberate choice of the delivery output.
84	
85	Source changes require review of affected/dependent rows, not automatic replacement
86	of all art. For a revised contract, reconcile pending work on its original connection,
87	retain the reviewed new packet, then use `plar prepare --revise --expect STATE_HASH`.
88	The new generation is appended to the existing store; prior inputs, jobs, candidates
89	and verdicts remain. Use returned IDs. Historical acceptance describes its original
90	contract and cannot complete the newly selected generation.

OUT = ROOT / "work/render-stage-pixl"
digest = lambda p: sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
prior = json.loads((ROOT / "work/queue.ready-reassessment/art-assessment.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
mine = json.loads((OUT / "measurements.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
fx = Image.open(ROOT / "assets/ready-confirmed.png").convert("RGBA")
px = fx.load()
out = {
    "prior_assessment_sha256": digest(ROOT / "work/queue.ready-reassessment/art-assessment.json"),
    "pixel_map_equal": prior["measured"]["pixel_map"] == mine["ready_fixture"]["pixel_map"],
    "transparent_pixel_rgba_values": sorted({px[x, y] for y in range(16) for x in range(16) if px[x, y][3] == 0}),
    "opaque_pixel_rgba_values": sorted({px[x, y] for y in range(16) for x in range(16) if px[x, y][3] != 0}),
    "contours": {},
    "prior_viewed_files": [],
    "diagnostics": {},
}
# per-row left/right edges for each arm (rows as in the fixture)
rows = {}
for y in range(16):
    xs = [x for x in range(16) if px[x, y][3]]
    if xs:
        rows[y] = xs
out["contours"]["right_arm_rows_4_to_9_left_edges"] = [min(x for x in rows[y] if x >= 7) for y in range(4, 10)]
out["contours"]["right_arm_rows_4_to_9_right_edges"] = [max(x for x in rows[y] if x >= 7) for y in range(4, 10)]
out["contours"]["left_arm_rows_8_to_12_left_edges"] = [min(rows[y]) for y in range(8, 13)]
out["contours"]["row_runs"] = mine["ready_fixture"]["row_runs"]
for v in prior["viewed"]:
    p = ROOT / v["path"]
    entry = {"path": v["path"], "claimed_sha256": v["sha256"], "exists": p.exists()}
    if p.exists():
        entry["actual_sha256"] = digest(p)
        entry["hash_matches"] = entry["actual_sha256"] == v["sha256"]
        with Image.open(p) as im:
            entry["size"] = list(im.size)
            entry["colors"] = sorted("#%02x%02x%02x a%d" % c for _, c in im.convert("RGBA").getcolors(65536))
    out["prior_viewed_files"].append(entry)
# do the earlier pixl inspection panel views equal the browser canvases?
cap = ROOT / "work/render-pixl-01"
insp = ROOT / ".pixl/assets/queue.ready/inspections/0126fe9615c7934b3e1ff0b197f769147de025c2a7064030dc2622199b90e38a/views"
for earlier, later in (("0001.png", "view-004.png"), ("0002.png", "view-005.png")):

rj_c = json.loads((caller / "render.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
rj_m = json.loads((cap / "render.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
diff_keys = [k for k in rj_m if rj_m[k] != rj_c.get(k)]
out["render_json_differing_top_level_keys"] = diff_keys
(OUT / "assessment-crosscheck.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out.items() if k != "prior_viewed_files"}, indent=1))
print(json.dumps([(e["path"].split("/")[-1], e.get("hash_matches"), e.get("colors")) for e in out["prior_viewed_files"]]))

"""Derive the proposed PLAR document from the current plar.txt without saving it (pixl_plar_save input + change ledger)."""
import copy
import json
import sys
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
OUT = ROOT / "work/render-stage-pixl"
digest = lambda p: sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
current_bytes = (ROOT / "plar.txt").read_bytes()
doc = json.loads(current_bytes)
base = copy.deepcopy(doc)
ledger = []


def change(entry_id, where, field, old, new, why, conditional=None):
    ledger.append({"id": entry_id, "where": where, "field": field, "old": old, "new": new, "why": why,
                   "hash_covered": field.split(".")[0] in ("requirements", "existing", "delivery", "depends_on", "consumers", "kind", "purpose", "references", "sources", "project"),
                   "conditional_on_style_adoption": bool(conditional), "if_not_adopted": conditional})
